To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a continuous-time model with heterogeneous agents can be represented as a static model with heterogeneous agents and (2) this representation is more realistic than a representative agent model.

the equilibrium interest rates in the heterogeneous-agent model are lower and more volatile, while the individual consumption growths rates are more dispersed, than in the representative consumer model.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a simple method to construct continuous-time models that are equivalent to their static counterparts.
the representative consumer is a good approximation of the economy if the risk aversion of the representative consumer is sufficiently high.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a continuous-time model, the representative consumer approach is not appropriate.
, in the absence of risk sharing, heterogeneous attitudes toward risk lead to a more volatile equilibrium interest rate and to more dispersed individual consumption growth rates.
the standard representative consumer model can be used as a good approximation of continuous-time models in which consumers have heterogeneous risk attitudes.
